events.name: The Marian Reforms
events.text: A great Italian city outside Roma now rivals the capital itself, and with it comes a general bold enough to remake the army. The old property rules are swept aside: landless citizens take the standard, the state arms them, and the manipular lines give way to standing cohorts sworn to their commander.

events.name: Death of a Philosopher
events.text: Word spreads from Athens that Epicurus has died in his garden, calm to the last. His followers gather quietly to honor a teacher who preached that a modest life, well shared, is the highest good.

events.name: The Census Rolls Are Read
events.text: The censors complete their count: hundreds of thousands of citizens fit to bear arms and pay their due. Tidier tax rolls put a little extra silver in the treasury.

events.name: Funeral Games in the Forum
events.text: At a nobleman's funeral in Roma, matched pairs of armed men fight before the crowd for the honor of the dead. The spectacle is grim, new, and wildly popular; it will not be the last.

events.name: A Play in the Latin Tongue
events.text: A freedman of Tarentum stages the first drama written in Latin rather than Greek. The crowds are delighted to laugh and weep in their own language, and the games gain a new fixture.

events.name: The Geometer of Syracuse Is Dead
events.text: Amid the sack of a great Sicilian city, a soldier cuts down an old man bent over his diagrams. Engineers everywhere mourn Archimedes, whose levers, screws, and burning wit held off a fleet.

events.name: The Night Rites Suppressed
events.text: Magistrates move against the secret nocturnal cult of the wine god, alleging conspiracy behind its torchlit rites. Thousands are arrested and the shrines are pulled down; the mood in the streets turns sullen and watchful.

events.name: A Comet Blazes
events.text: A long-tailed star hangs in the evening sky for weeks, and no two soothsayers agree on its meaning. Kings consult their priests; the common folk bar their doors and wait.

events.name: New Veins of Silver
events.text: Prospectors report rich new silver workings in the hill country, and the smelters burn day and night. Mine leases and royalties briefly swell every treasury that touches the trade.

events.name: Games of a New Age
events.text: Heralds proclaim festivals such as no living man has seen and none will see again: three days and nights of sacrifice, theatre, and song to mark the turning of an age. The expense is enormous and nobody minds.

events.name: The Republic Divided
events.text: Word runs through every forum: a great house has raised its standards against the Senate itself. Brother watches brother, and the markets are afraid.

events.name: Master of the Middle Sea
events.text: One power now holds more of the world than any other in living memory. Merchants reroute, kings take note, and the crowds cheer whoever feeds them the news.

events.name: The Shadow Over All Thrones
events.text: Thirty lands under one banner. Every remaining court in the world now drafts the same letter: what do we do about them?

disasters.name: Aetna Burns
disasters.text: Rivers of fire crawl down from Aetna's summit through vineyard and grove. The islanders say the giant beneath the mountain has turned in his sleep.

disasters.name: Earthquake in Anatolia
disasters.text: The ground heaves along the old fault lines of Asia, throwing down colonnades and city walls alike. Survivors dig through the rubble as the aftershocks roll on.

disasters.name: Earthquake in the Levant
disasters.text: A shudder runs the length of the coast road, toppling warehouses in the ports and cracking the great temple platforms. Caravans arrive to find the markets in ruins.

disasters.name: The Nile Rises Too High
disasters.text: The inundation the farmers pray for comes this year as a torrent, drowning dykes, granaries, and mud-brick villages together. The priests promise rich soil next season to those who live to till it.

disasters.name: The Padus Breaks Its Banks
disasters.text: Autumn rains in the mountains send the great river spilling brown across the plain. Farmsteads stand roof-deep, and the roads north are mud for a season.

disasters.name: Storms off the Northern Coasts
disasters.text: Weeks of gales scour the grey channel coasts, driving ships ashore and stripping roofs from the fishing towns. The old men say the sea gods take their tithe in winter.
